How exact coverage works in Beacon Lattice

How five distinct rotatable pentominoes tile Beacon Lattice’s five-by-five board exactly once, and what makes a placement invalid.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 19, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Cover every cell. Overlap nothing.

Play Beacon LatticeBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: In current Beacon Lattice, “exact cover” means fitting five five-cell pieces over all 25 squares with no overlap and no gap. It is not a board of 0, 1, and 2+ coverage counters.

The game starts with an empty five-by-five lattice and five different pentominoes named F, V, I, U, and L. Each piece covers five connected squares. Five pieces times five squares gives 25, so a completed layout must use every piece once and cover every square exactly once.

Choose a shape, rotation, and anchor

Select one remaining piece, rotate it in quarter turns, and choose an anchor row and column. The shape keeps its identity; the current controls provide rotation, not reflection. You can set the coordinates with the labeled selectors and place button, or activate an uncovered board square as the anchor.

A placement is accepted only when all five cells fit inside the board and are still empty. An out-of-bounds placement or overlap leaves the board and inventory unchanged. The status message explains the rejection.

Why gaps and overlaps matter

A partial board is not a solved board. After each accepted placement, inspect the uncovered regions and the shapes still in the inventory. A narrow leftover area may rule out several pieces; a corner or edge can reduce the number of orientations that fit. If the final piece is used while any square remains uncovered, the attempt ends as a loss. Every cell covered with all five pieces is a win.

Read the current progress display

The board labels covered squares with a beacon number, while uncovered squares remain visibly empty. The status and progress display report placements and remaining pieces—not a per-cell coverage count, a stored best, or an inventory of locked beacons. Undo removes the last accepted placement and returns that piece to the inventory; reset restores the same empty starting task.

For placement reasoning, see How to reason about Beacon Lattice placements. The game page is the source for current controls.
